Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

If the node-set is empty, an empty string is returned." Diagnosis:
The failure in the test org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMModelTest.testUnion() reveals that the union operation on XPath node-sets is not returning nodes sorted in document order. Specifically, the test selecting union of contact nodes expects "John" (likely the first in document order), but the actual returned value does not respect this order. The bug report clarifies that the union operation returns nodes in an order that is not consistent with the document order specification from XPath: the string() function should use the string-value of the first node in document order from the node-set.

From the inspected code snippets:
- CoreOperationUnion.computeValue(EvalContext) creates a UnionContext from EvalContexts of all arguments.
- UnionContext constructor initializes with an array of EvalContexts, presumably each representing parts of the union node-sets.
- UnionContext.getDocumentOrder() returns 1 if it contains more than one context; otherwise delegates to super.getDocumentOrder(). This simplistic approach does not appear to merge or sort nodes from the multiple contexts by their document order, but rather just returns a constant in many cases.

The problem is likely that the union context is constructed from multiple EvalContexts without merging or sorting their nodes by document order. This means the union result is not in document order as required by XPath semantics.

The incorrect ordering ultimately causes the string() function to pick the wrong node value, causing the testUnion failure.

Recent bug reports mentioning binary operators and node-set comparisons being incorrect support the idea that node-sets are not handled or combined correctly in operations.

Summary:
The root cause is that the union operation represented by CoreOperationUnion and implemented by UnionContext does not produce a merged and document-ordered node-set but instead returns nodes in an unsorted combined context array, violating XPath document-order requirements.

The fix should involve modifying how UnionContext merges and sorts nodes from the multiple EvalContexts so that the resulting node-set respects document order. This will ensure string()/value() functions behave correctly on unions.

Recommended methods for fix investigation:
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.CoreOperationUnion.computeValue(org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.EvalContext)
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.axes.UnionContext (constructor and methods responsible for combining nodes and document order)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
